inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report (English) consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment transactions' 56 (restricted-stock plan introduced FY2026); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed; effectively an SBC-zero filer
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of treasury shares 20,005 (financing activities). Board resolved 14-May-2026 a further buyback of up to 25.0m shares / 50.0bn yen, 1-Jun-2026 to 31-Mar-2027, with cancellation. Count held FLAT at the 31-Mar-2026 figure: the buyback is funded from the same cash pile the bridge adds back, so it is value-neutral near IV (shares and cash fall together). The FY2027 EPS guidance of 109.49 yen on 34.0bn net income implies ~310.5m shares, consistent with this basis.
inputs.share_count_basis: 310,690,987 shares issued excluding treasury shares at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 Annual Report, treasury-share note); diluted EPS not presented because there are no potential ordinary shares, so basic = fully diluted
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Latest balance sheet with line detail is 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 annual). The Q1 FY2027 (June 2026) presentation carries no balance sheet; H1 FY2027 (Sep 2026) results are due 12-Nov-2026 and should refresh cash, borrowings and the share count (buyback in progress). Net cash will be lower at Sep-2026 by roughly the buyback and dividends paid since March, which is the value-neutral mechanism noted above.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built rate: 10y JGB ~1.6%, Japan ERP ~6%, beta ~1.1 for a large-cap machine-tool maker with a 69% equity ratio and net cash -> cost of equity ~8.3-8.6%; negligible debt weight. WACC 8.5% in every scenario; cyclicality is charged in the scenario paths and the bear weight, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 filer. Lease payments (principal 3,276 in financing + lease interest, ~0.8% of revenue) are charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (12,463 at 31-Mar-2026, inside 'other financial liabilities') are EXCLUDED from net debt, so total_debt is bonds and borrowings only (72,800 current + 8,000 non-current). da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2026 total D&A 22,843 less ~3.0bn ROU ~= 19.8bn = 4.5% of revenue), so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests (4,891 at 31-Mar-2026, profit share 203 in FY2026) deducted ONCE in the equity bridge.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received 1,198 stripped because net cash (72.8bn) exceeds the owner-FCF base (43.9bn); the cash is added back in the bridge instead. Finance income of 4,043 also contains FX gains, which are not stripped (they are not a return on the bridged cash). Dividends received (65) left in the flows and the FVOCI investment-securities portfolio left out of the bridge: immaterial and conservative.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon (FY2027-FY2036), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied (JPY WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, interest income stripped, SBC-zero market). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF. FY LABELS: this repo's FY2026 = year ended 31-Mar-2026 = Amada's own 'FY2025'; the company's 'FY2026 forecast' is our FY2027 (year ending Mar-2027). OWNER FCF FY0: reported FCF 48,466 (OCF 58,065 - PP&E 5,578 - intangibles 4,021) less SBC 56 less interest received 1,198 less lease principal 3,276 = 43,936 (10.0% of revenue). The engine's own year-1 build ties: EBITDA 15.5% - lease 0.8% - D&A ex-ROU 4.5% = EBIT ~10.2% of revenue vs reported OP margin 10.2%. PEAK-CYCLE CAUTION: revenue, orders (456.9bn FY2026; Q1 FY2027 orders +78% incl. front-loaded AI/semiconductor orders management expects to peak mid-year) are at records, but EBITDA margin (15.5%) is BELOW the FY2016-2026 average (~16.9%) and the FY2022-24 range (18-18.6%) because of US tariffs, personnel costs and acquisition amortisation; so the peak risk sits in volume, not margin. Every scenario therefore scripts an explicit downcycle in years 3-4 rather than compounding from the record base; mid-cycle margins are set at the decade average, not the FY2022-24 highs. Terminal cap multiple 14x FCF (cyclical) in base, 15x bull, 12x bear. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a. Cash tax 34% vs 30.6% statutory to absorb non-deductible acquisition-intangible amortisation (share deals, no tax step-up) and the ~35-38% cash/pre-tax ratio actually paid in FY2024-26. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventories (316bn) far above payables + advances (103bn), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -20% of the revenue change (releases cash in the scripted downturn, symmetrically).

equity_bridge.note: 31-Mar-2026 balance sheet; flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.7% diverges >30% from revenue 11.8% and EPS 12.6%: the 5-year window runs from the FY2021 cyclical trough (revenue 250bn) to a record FY2026 (437bn, incl. ~45bn of acquired revenue and yen weakness), so revenue/EPS CAGRs are trough-to-peak and not a forward proxy. The 3-yr EPS CAGR is negative because margins compressed while revenue grew.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal. FY2021 owner FCF ~34.7bn -> FY2026 43.9bn = 4.8% CAGR. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined: FY2023 owner FCF was ~-3.7bn (OCF 24.9bn absorbed by a 40bn+ working-capital build as revenue rose 17%). SBC is immaterial so the owner and reported series diverge only by interest and leases.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue 468bn (+7%), a modest beat of the 460bn guidance given Q1 +30% and record orders; OP ~49bn vs 48bn guided. FY2028 +3% as front-loaded AI/semiconductor orders roll through. FY2029-30 scripted downcycle (-5%, -2%) with EBITDA margin dipping to 14-14.5% (resilient, as in FY2017/FY2020, not a 2009-style collapse). Recovery to 16.5% mid-cycle margin by FY2033, the FY2016-2026 average, below the FY2022-24 18%+ highs. Capex glides from guidance 2.4% toward 3.8% of revenue as the current under-investment relative to D&A normalises; D&A ex-ROU eases from 4.4% to 4.0% as acquired-intangible amortisation rolls off.

bull.narrative: AI/data-center enclosure and cooling demand proves a multi-year layer, the Electronics Process unit (Via Mechanics) inflects to high-margin advanced-packaging revenue from H2 FY2027, automation mix keeps rising on skilled-labour shortages, and the FY2029-30 cycle is a pause (+2%, 0%) rather than a contraction. Margins recover to the FY2022-24 18% band by FY2033 as tariff refunds, pricing and manufacturing rationalisation stick.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands near guidance on tariff-refund and FX help, then hyperscaler capex rolls over in FY2028 and auto/EV stays weak: revenue -8% and -10% (FY2021 was -22%) with EBITDA margin troughing at 10.5% (FY2017/20-style compression plus negative operating leverage and EP-unit losses). Chinese low-cost entrants (Yawei) hold the mid-market share they took, so recovery margin tops out at 14.5%, below the decade average; terminal growth 1.5% and a 12x cap reflect a lower-quality cycle.

scenario_narratives.base: The axes for Amada are (1) whether the AI/data-center enclosure, rack and switchgear capex that drove record FY2026 orders persists or front-loads, (2) whether the H&F and Via Mechanics acquisitions reach the margin management promised (the Electronics Process unit lost money in Q1 FY2027 on amortisation and low-margin carryover work), (3) the ordinary machine-tool capex cycle, which Amada has never escaped (-22% revenue in FY2021), and (4) tariff/FX. Base: FY2027 beats guidance modestly, a conventional downcycle arrives in FY2029-30 and the company earns its decade-average 16.5% EBITDA margin mid-cycle. Revenue compounds only ~2.4%/yr over the horizon because it starts from a record year.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI/data-center demand layers durably on top of the fabrication base, Via Mechanics' advanced-packaging orders convert from H2 FY2027, automation penetration keeps lifting mix, and the next downcycle is a flat patch rather than a contraction; margins return to the 18% FY2022-24 band.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex rolls over in FY2028 while auto/EV and general fabrication stay soft; two-year revenue contraction with margin compression to 10.5%; acquisitions dilute rather than lift returns; Chinese price competition caps the recovery margin at 14.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the starting point is a record order book that management itself says is front-loaded by AI/semiconductor orders peaking mid-FY2027, and the FY2026 OP guidance was already missed once on tariffs and costs; there is no solvency or refinancing risk (net cash, 69% equity ratio), which is why the bear is not higher. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: a durable AI capex layer, the EP unit's unproven margin inflection, and a benign next cycle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a Japanese cyclical machine-tool maker at a record-revenue, below-average-margin point in its cycle. The model refuses to compound from the record base: every scenario carries an explicit downcycle, mid-cycle margins are the decade average rather than recent highs, capex normalises up toward D&A, and interest on the 72.8bn net cash is stripped from the flows and the cash added back once in the bridge. SBC is immaterial, so house and street coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-cycle extrapolation: FY2026 revenue and orders are records partly on front-loaded AI/semiconductor orders and ~45bn of acquired revenue; if the FY2029-30 downcycle scripted here arrives earlier or deeper, the base case is too generous
Margin path: the base assumes recovery to 16.5% EBITDA; FY2026 printed 15.5% with tariffs, personnel costs and acquisition amortisation still rising
Acquisition integration: H&F and Via Mechanics (~69bn, goodwill 31.1bn) have not yet shown the promised margin; EP unit loss-making in Q1 FY2027

Working capital: 316bn of receivables and inventories against 103bn of payables and advances; a -20% capture on revenue change is an estimate and the FY2023 build (owner FCF ~-3.7bn) shows how large the swing can be

Balance-sheet vintage: net cash and share count are from 31-Mar-2026; the 50bn buyback and dividends since then reduce both cash and shares (value-neutral near IV, but the H1 FY2027 filing on 12-Nov-2026 should refresh them)
FX: 64% of sales overseas; FY2027 guidance assumes USD/JPY 150, EUR/JPY 175; yen strength is a translation and margin headwind
